D-1 REVISION DIRECTIVE — PERSIST UNTIL SATISFIED. The matching upper theorem is mathematically reachable under the proposal’s existing assumptions; do not demote it again to an OEQ and do not substitute the conservative guarded frontier. Promote the full score-cell conditional likelihood-ratio construction to a main theorem for PN, with the treatment/outcome-swapped analogue for PS. Use a randomized Feldman–Cousins/Neyman profile-likelihood-ratio inversion in the cross-fitted full score-cell experiment: conditional on each fold’s training sample, validation covariates, and common-cell component, retain all four \((A,Y)\) cells and their score marks, model the score-bearing indicators by their joint conditional Poisson-binomial experiment, profile the cell intensities over the existing overlap/Hölder class, and calibrate the LR statistic by its least-favorable conditional law; its bounded-\(nd_n\) limit is the corresponding marked-Poisson LR experiment. If the factual count is zero, define the inversion as \([0,1]\); for bounded \(nd_n\), use randomized discrete critical values and permit a nonshrinking set; for \(nd_n\to\infty\), prove conditional LAN, Gaussian LR recovery, and equality of the resulting influence function with Tian–Wu’s efficient monotone-PN influence function. Fix an admissible slowly diverging transition, e.g. \(\kappa_n=\log n\), so the already specified spline rates give \(\sqrt{\kappa_n}r_{e,n},\sqrt{\kappa_n}r_{0,n}\to0\), and state explicitly the nuisance-stability hypotheses already present: fixed-fold cross-fitting, overlap and clipping, rare localization, the Hölder/design spline rates, the score envelope and rare-scale variance bounds, and the displayed rate-compatibility condition on \(nd_n>\kappa_n\). The theorem must state, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\),
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_n}P\{\theta(P)\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR}}_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha,\qquad
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_n}
\frac{E_P[\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR}}_{n,\alpha})]}
{\min\{1,[n d(P)]^{-1/2}\}}\le C_\alpha<\infty,
\]
with the same assertions for PS, and pair this with the least-favorable lower theorem so that every uniformly honest \(D_n\) satisfies the matching normalized lower bound; explicitly record that \(nd_n\to\lambda<\infty\) therefore yields nonshrinking expected diameter. Complete all round-3 hygiene repairs in the same revision: fit \(m_0\) only on control training observations (or by the exactly equivalent control-weighted regression); define \(\mathcal M_n\) as the observed-law projection of a full-data class satisfying consistency, ignorability, monotonicity, and overlap; certify least-favorable membership by stating \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), \(\varepsilon\le1/2\le1-\varepsilon\), \(C_\omega\ge1\), \(2\bar d\le1\), and Hölder radii large enough to contain the constants \(e\equiv1/2\) and \(m_0\equiv2(1-t)d_n\); replace every supremum whose right side depends on \(P\) by either a pointwise-for-every-\(P\) statement or the normalized supremum above; and correct the literature attribution so McGrath–Burke motivates rare-binomial coverage/relative-margin comparisons while Huwang supplies the nonuniform normal-approximation failure claim.

The construction needs no crux-encoding strengthening because the finite-information region does not require consistent point estimation: exact randomized inversion of the conditional discrete experiment supplies honesty and a diameter of constant order, which is precisely the minimax order when \(nd_n=O(1)\), including the zero-count event. In the transition region, rare localization makes the score-bearing cell intensities order \(d_n\), while the existing polynomial nuisance rates dominate a logarithmic \(\kappa_n\); above that transition, the proposal’s existing rate-compatibility condition makes cross-fit intensity drift negligible relative to \(\sqrt{d_n/n}\). Conditional LR curvature is then order \(nd_n\), giving diameter \(O((nd_n)^{-1/2})\), and its LAN expansion reproduces the Tian–Wu efficient Gaussian limit. Combined with the certified least-favorable Poisson submodel, this supplies both sides of the claimed honest minimax frontier rather than merely a harder proof of the guarded \(\sqrt{\kappa_n}\)-inflated bound.

directive:
SUPERSEDING D-1 DIRECTIVE — PERSIST UNTIL SATISFIED. Replace every earlier D-1 instruction for `stat_pn_weak_event_honest_inference`. Preserve the locked PN/PS kernel, causal model, and standard assumptions, but do not present the novel upper frontier as proved: in the D-1 proposal label the randomized PN/PS likelihood-ratio frontier `Conjecture 1 (NOT YET PROVED)`, retain it as the mandatory lead D0 solve target, and require D0 either to prove it under the declared class or to state precisely which claimed coverage, diameter, Poisson, or LAN conclusion fails. Do not demote it to an open-ended question and do not call it a theorem before that proof exists.

Define an admissible full-data extension by
\[
\widetilde P_n\in\mathcal P\{(X,A,Y(0),Y(1))\},\qquad
P_n=\widetilde P_n\circ(X,A,Y(A))^{-1},
\]
and define the causal targets only under \(\widetilde P_n\):
\[
\theta(\widetilde P_n)=\widetilde P_n\{Y(0)=0\mid A=1,Y(1)=1\},\qquad
\vartheta(\widetilde P_n)=\widetilde P_n\{Y(1)=1\mid A=0,Y(0)=0\}.
\]
Under consistency, conditional ignorability, monotonicity, and overlap, prove
\[
\theta(\widetilde P_n)=\Theta_{\rm PN}(P_n)
=1-\frac{E_{P_n}[e_n(X)m_{0,n}(X)]}
{E_{P_n}[e_n(X)m_{1,n}(X)]},
\]
\[
\vartheta(\widetilde P_n)=\Theta_{\rm PS}(P_n)
=1-\frac{E_{P_n}[(1-e_n(X))(1-m_{1,n}(X))]}
{E_{P_n}[(1-e_n(X))(1-m_{0,n}(X))]}.
\]
State explicitly that these equalities make both targets extension-invariant: any two admitted full-data extensions with observed marginal \(P_n\) have the same PN and PS values. Retain
\[
d_n^{\rm PN}=E_{P_n}[AY],\qquad d_n^{\rm PS}=E_{P_n}[(1-A)(1-Y)]
\]
and preserve exactly the user’s PN score
\[
\psi_{t,n}(O;\eta)
=A\{Y-m_0(X)\}
-\frac{e(X)}{1-e(X)}(1-A)\{Y-m_0(X)\}
-tAY .
\]

Replace the presently verbal “score-cell LR” by the following measurable finite/sieve construction. For deterministic spline bases \(B_{e,n},B_{0,n}\) of the already specified dimensions and deterministic compact coefficient boxes expanding slowly enough to contain Hölder approximants, set
\[
e_\beta(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]}
\{B_{e,n}(x)^\top\beta\},\quad
m_{0,\gamma}(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]}
\{B_{0,n}(x)^\top\gamma\}.
\]
At the observed covariate values introduce \(u_i=m_1(X_i)\in[0,1]\), empirical-likelihood weights \(w=(w_1,\ldots,w_n)\in\Delta_n\), and
\[
q_{i,11}=e_\beta(X_i)u_i,\quad q_{i,10}=e_\beta(X_i)(1-u_i),\quad
q_{i,01}=(1-e_\beta(X_i))m_{0,\gamma}(X_i),\quad
q_{i,00}=(1-e_\beta(X_i))(1-m_{0,\gamma}(X_i)).
\]
The compact profiling domain \(\Xi_n\) must impose \(m_{0,\gamma}(X_i)\le u_i\), \(0\le d(w,\beta,u)=\sum_iw_i e_\beta(X_i)u_i\le\bar d\), and
\[
e_\beta(X_i)u_i\le C_\omega d(w,\beta,u)
\]
for every \(i\), together with the declared overlap and coefficient restrictions. Define
\[
L_n(w,\beta,\gamma,u)
=\prod_{i=1}^n w_iq_{i,A_iY_i},
\]
and the PN null domain
\[
\Xi_n(t)=\left\{\xi\in\Xi_n:
\sum_{i=1}^nw_i e_\beta(X_i)
\bigl[(1-t)u_i-m_{0,\gamma}(X_i)\bigr]=0\right\}.
\]
This is the finite/sieve version of \(E_P\psi_{t,n}(O;\eta_n)=0\); the four score-cell marks obtained from the displayed user kernel are deterministic functions of \((X_i,A_i,Y_i)\) and the off-fold fits and must be retained rather than replacing the raw cells. Define
\[
\Lambda_n(t)=2\left\{\sup_{\xi\in\Xi_n}\log L_n(\xi)
-\sup_{\xi\in\Xi_n(t)}\log L_n(\xi)\right\},
\]
using fixed conventions for empty null sets and zero likelihoods. For any threshold \(s\), select the least-favorable null law as the lexicographically first maximizer
\[
\xi^{\rm LF}_{n,t,s}\in
\arg\max_{\xi\in\Xi_n(t)}
P_\xi\{\Lambda_n^{*}(t)\ge s\};
\]
compactness, a fixed tie-break, and enumeration of the finite support followed by global optimization over \(\Xi_n(t)\) make this a defined computable selector. With one independent \(U\sim{\rm Unif}(0,1)\), define
\[
p_n(t;Z,U)=
\sup_{\xi\in\Xi_n(t)}
\left[
P_\xi\{\Lambda_n^{*}(t)>\Lambda_n(t;Z)\}
+U\,P_\xi\{\Lambda_n^{*}(t)=\Lambda_n(t;Z)\}
\right],
\]
and
\[
\mathcal C^{\rm LR,PN}_{n,\alpha}
=\{t\in[0,1]:p_n(t;Z,U)>\alpha\},
\]
with \(\mathcal C^{\rm LR,PN}_{n,\alpha}=[0,1]\) when \(N_{11,n}=0\). Require the optimization maps to be Borel and define the set by this Borel \(p\)-value map, not by an unspecified continuum inversion. Obtain PS by applying the identical construction to \((X,1-A,1-Y)\).

The inner likelihood conditional on fixed covariates is explicitly the Poisson-binomial/four-cell product \(\prod_iq_{i,A_iY_i}\); the weights \(w_i\) are mandatory because the causal null is a marginal, not a conditional-on-\(X\), restriction. Do not claim that conditioning jointly on “every fold’s training sample” defines a likelihood: the complements of cross-fitting folds collectively reveal the entire sample. Condition foldwise only when proving cross-fit remainder bounds, or use an independently trained nuisance fit; the displayed unconditional empirical-likelihood layer must carry the random-\(X\) component. A procedure conditioning away validation covariates without this layer cannot recover the full Tian–Wu influence function unless the additional, currently absent restriction
\[
E\{\psi_{\theta_n,n}(O;\eta_n)\mid X\}=0\quad\text{a.s.}
\]
is imposed.

Delete the logarithmic guard from the LAN claim. The minimal required condition along every sequence \(n d_n^{\rm PN}\to\infty\) is the uniform rare-scale cross-fit remainder
\[
\sup_{t\in[0,1]}
\left|
\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i\in I_{k,n}}
\bigl[
\psi_{t,n}(O_i;\widehat\eta_{-k,n})
-\psi_{t,n}(O_i;\eta_n)
\bigr]
\right|
=o_{P_n}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{d_n^{\rm PN}}n}\right),
\]
uniformly over the declared model class. A sufficient rate formulation, to be derived rather than assumed silently, is
\[
\frac{r_{0,n}}{\sqrt{d_n^{\rm PN}}}
+\sqrt{\frac{n}{d_n^{\rm PN}}}\,r_{e,n}r_{0,n}=o(1),
\qquad r_{e,n}=o(1),
\]
with rare-response/localization refinements permitted if the ordinary spline rate is too crude. D0 must verify this condition for every diverging effective-count sequence, including \(n d_n=o(\log n)\); if the specified learners cannot do so, the all-sequence LAN claim must be withdrawn or the exact failing sequence exhibited. Under this remainder and score nondegeneracy, D0 must prove LAN at scale \(\sqrt{nd_n}\), identify the influence function as \(d_n^{-1}\psi_{\theta_n,n}\), and verify equality with the Tian–Wu monotone-PN efficient influence function.

Include the following no-covariate exhibit. In the certified least-favorable submodel \(e=1/2\),
\[
(p_{11},p_{01},p_{10},p_{00})
=\left(d,(1-t)d,\frac12-d,\frac12-(1-t)d\right),
\]
so
\[
L(t,d)\propto
d^{N_{11}}\{(1-t)d\}^{N_{01}}
(1/2-d)^{N_{10}}\{1/2-(1-t)d\}^{N_{00}},
\quad 0\le d\le\bar d,
\]
and, conditional on \(M=N_{11}+N_{01}\),
\[
N_{01}\mid M\sim{\rm Binomial}\!\left(M,q_t\right),
\qquad q_t=\frac{1-t}{2-t}.
\]
For \((N_{11},N_{01},N_{10},N_{00})=(2,1,8,9)\), \(M=3\), \(\widehat q=1/3\), and \(\widehat t=(1-2\widehat q)/(1-\widehat q)=1/2\). Display
\[
\Lambda(t)=2\left[
\log\frac{1/3}{q_t}
+2\log\frac{2/3}{1-q_t}
\right],
\]
enumerate \(j=0,1,2,3\) under \({\rm Binomial}(3,q_t)\), and apply the same randomized upper-tail rule to obtain the accepted \(t\)’s; verify that \(N_{11}=0\) invokes \([0,1]\) and that all likelihood denominators are nonzero.

Conjecture 1 must state uniform \(1-\alpha\) coverage and expected-diameter order \(\min\{1,(nd_n)^{-1/2}\}\) for PN and PS, with a nonshrinking marked-Poisson boundary when \(nd_n\to\lambda<\infty\), and must be paired with the certified least-favorable lower bound. D0 must prove the sieve/empirical-likelihood approximation, least-favorable calibration, diameter bound, Poisson limit, and all-sequence LAN result. No claim of exact finite-sample validity over the original continuous nonparametric class is permitted: the finite procedure is exact only for its finite profiling experiment, while transfer to the declared class is part of Conjecture 1.

The obstruction requiring the empirical-likelihood layer is exact: the marginal null \(E\psi_t=0\) does not imply a conditional null given validation covariates, because generally \(E(\psi_{\theta_n}\mid X)\neq0\); conditioning on \(X\) therefore discards a component of the efficient variance. Moreover, conditioning simultaneously on every cross-fitting training complement conditions on the whole dataset and degenerates the purported experiment. The finite/sieve likelihood above preserves the four-cell Poisson-binomial component while restoring the random-\(X\) law and a measurable least-favorable inversion. The unguarded rare-scale remainder is precisely what makes nuisance drift negligible relative to the oracle fluctuation \(\sqrt{d_n/n}\); without it, LAN for sequences such as \(nd_n=o(\log n)\) is unsupported.

(1) **SUPERSEDING D-1 ROOT-FIX DIRECTIVE — PERSIST UNTIL SATISFIED.** Preserve the PN/PS causal assumptions, identified functionals, and target frontier \(\min\{1,(nd_n)^{-1/2}\}\), but delete `ass:rare-scale-remainder` and do not encode that frontier through any estimator-dependent model assumption. Replace it by the primitive observed-law class with fixed \(p,\beta_e,\beta_0>0\): bounded design density \(c_X\le f_X\le C_X\), overlap \(\varepsilon\le e\le1-\varepsilon\), \(e\in\mathcal H^{\beta_e}(L_e)\), \(m_0\in\mathcal H^{\beta_0}(L_0)\), and an admitted full-data extension satisfying consistency, ignorability, and monotonicity. Delete `ass:rare-localization`: monotonicity and overlap already imply
\[
m_0(x)\le m_1(x),\qquad E[m_0(X)]\le E[m_1(X)]\le d_n/\varepsilon,
\]
which is the weakest localization needed below; no bound on \(\|e m_1/d_n\|_\infty\) is required.

Use the following named learner: fixed-\(K\)-fold, clipped tensor-product B-spline sieve ERM. For \(j\in\{e,0\}\), take spline degree \(r_j\ge\lceil\beta_j\rceil\), \(K_{j,n}\asymp(n/\log n)^{1/(2\beta_j+p)}\) equally spaced interior knots per coordinate, and
\[
J_{j,n}=(K_{j,n}+r_j+1)^p\asymp(n/\log n)^{p/(2\beta_j+p)}.
\]
On each training complement, fit \(e\) by Bernoulli logistic loss
\[
\widehat\beta_{e,-k}\in\arg\min_\beta
\sum_{i\notin I_k}\{-A_i\log e_\beta(X_i)-(1-A_i)\log[1-e_\beta(X_i)]\},
\]
and fit \(m_0\) by control-weighted squared loss
\[
\widehat\gamma_{0,-k}\in\arg\min_\gamma
\sum_{i\notin I_k}(1-A_i)\{Y_i-B_{0,n}(X_i)^\top\gamma\}^2.
\]
Use deterministic compact coefficient boxes containing the Hölder approximants, and clip the fitted functions to \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) and \([0,1]\). Uniformly over the primitive class, this learner has
\[
a_{e,n}:=\|\widehat e-e\|_{2,P}\vee\|\widehat e-e\|_{\infty}
=O_P\!\left[(\log n/n)^{s_e}\right],\quad
a_{0,n}:=\|\widehat m_0-m_0\|_{2,P}
=O_P\!\left[(\log n/n)^{s_0}\right],
\]
where \(s_e=\beta_e/(2\beta_e+p)\) and \(s_0=\beta_0/(2\beta_0+p)\).

Derive, rather than assume, the cross-fit remainder. Writing \(\delta_e=\widehat e-e\), \(\delta_0=\widehat m_0-m_0\), direct score algebra gives
\[
E\!\left[\psi_t(O;\widehat\eta)-\psi_t(O;\eta)\mid\widehat\eta\right]
=E\!\left[\frac{\delta_e(X)\delta_0(X)}{1-\widehat e(X)}\right],
\]
independently of \(t\), and
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\psi_t(O;\widehat\eta)-\psi_t(O;\eta)\mid\widehat\eta\right)
\lesssim a_{0,n}^2+d_n a_{e,n}^2.
\]
The \(d_na_{e,n}^2\) term follows from \(E[m_0]\le d_n/\varepsilon\) and the propensity sup-norm rate. Hence
\[
\sup_{t\in[0,1]}\left|\mathbb P_n\{\psi_t(\widehat\eta)-\psi_t(\eta)\}\right|
=O_P\!\left(
\frac{a_{0,n}}{\sqrt n}
+\sqrt{\frac{d_n}{n}}\,a_{e,n}
+a_{e,n}a_{0,n}\right).
\]
It is \(o_P(\sqrt{d_n/n})\) exactly in the characterized Gaussian sub-regime
\[
a_{0,n}=o(\sqrt{d_n}),\qquad
\sqrt{\frac n{d_n}}\,a_{e,n}a_{0,n}=o(1),
\]
equivalently
\[
d_n\gg
\max\!\left\{
(\log n/n)^{2s_0},
\ n(\log n/n)^{2(s_e+s_0)}
\right\}.
\tag{G}
\]
A nonempty fixed-smoothness Gaussian regime therefore requires \(s_e+s_0>1/2\). For \(d_n=n^{-b}\), ignoring only the displayed logarithmic boundary, (G) is
\[
0\le b<\min\{1,\ 2s_0,\ 2(s_e+s_0)-1\}.
\]
Withdraw every claim that all \(nd_n\to\infty\) sequences are covered.

State the honest split. First, on the finite empirical-support experiment defined below, randomized least-favorable LR inversion has exact uniform \(1-\alpha\) coverage for every count; when \(nd_n=O(1)\), its diameter is at most one and the certified two-point submodel gives a nonshrinking lower bound, hence the constant-order rare-count frontier and marked-Poisson limit are valid there. Exactness is only for this finite experiment, not automatically for the original continuous law. Second, over the original Hölder law class, prove efficient Gaussian recovery and \(O((nd_n)^{-1/2})\) diameter only under (G), score nondegeneracy at the true target, and the required sieve/empirical-likelihood transfer. Outside bounded \(nd_n\) and (G), retain coverage conservatively by \([0,1]\), but make no matching shrinking-diameter claim. Any assertion that one LR construction attains the frontier throughout the intervening \(nd_n\to\infty\) regime remains explicitly a conjecture requiring a new adaptive or higher-order argument.

Fully define the finite experiment. Given the observed covariate array \(x_{1:n}\), retain index labels even when covariates repeat and set
\[
\Omega_z=(\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{00,01,10,11\})^n.
\]
For \(\xi=(w,\beta,\gamma,u)\), require \(w\in\Delta_n\), \(u_i\in[0,1]\), \(u_i=u_j\) whenever \(x_i=x_j\), \(m_{0,\gamma}(x_i)\le u_i\), and
\[
d(\xi)=\sum_iw_i e_\beta(x_i)u_i\in[0,\bar d].
\]
Do not reintroduce pointwise rare localization. Define
\[
q_{i,11}=e_\beta(x_i)u_i,\quad q_{i,10}=e_\beta(x_i)(1-u_i),\quad
q_{i,01}=(1-e_\beta(x_i))m_{0,\gamma}(x_i),\quad
q_{i,00}=(1-e_\beta(x_i))(1-m_{0,\gamma}(x_i)),
\]
and, for \(S=((L_j,C_j))_{j=1}^n\in\Omega_z\),
\[
P_\xi(S)=\prod_{j=1}^n w_{L_j}q_{L_j,C_j}.
\]
Thus empirical weights govern resampled support labels; identical covariate values may recur through distinct labels, and simulated samples may repeat or omit labels. The null set is
\[
\Xi_n(t)=\left\{\xi:
\sum_iw_i e_\beta(x_i)\big[(1-t)u_i-m_{0,\gamma}(x_i)\big]=0\right\}.
\]
For each original label \(i\), fold \(k(i)\), cell \(c=(a,y)\), and \(t\), freeze the mark map
\[
h_{i,c}(t)=\psi_t((x_i,a,y);\widehat\eta_{-k(i)}).
\]
A simulated observation \((L_j,C_j)\) carries the newly simulated mark \(h_{L_j,C_j}(t)\), never the observed unit’s realized mark. Define
\[
\ell_\xi(S)=\sum_j\{\log w_{L_j}+\log q_{L_j,C_j}\},
\quad
\Lambda_n^*(t;S)=2\left[
\sup_{\xi\in\Xi_n}\ell_\xi(S)
-\sup_{\xi\in\Xi_n(t)}\ell_\xi(S)\right],
\]
with fixed conventions \(\log0=-\infty\) and \(\sup\varnothing=-\infty\). The observed statistic is this same map evaluated at \(S_{\rm obs}=((i,A_iY_i))_{i=1}^n\). Raw cells determine the likelihood; the simulated marks remain attached coordinates used in the score/LAN expansion.

For \(s\in[0,\infty]\), define the least-favorable selector by
\[
\xi^{\rm LF}_{n,t,s}
=\operatorname{lexmin}\arg\max_{\xi\in\Xi_n(t)}
P_\xi\{\Lambda_n^*(t)\ge s\}.
\]
Because \(\Omega_z\) is finite and \(\Xi_n(t)\) is compact, the tail probability is a finite Borel function; invoke the measurable maximum theorem and the fixed lexicographic selector. With independent \(U\sim{\rm Unif}(0,1)\), set
\[
p_n(t;S_{\rm obs},U)=
\sup_{\xi\in\Xi_n(t)}
\left[
P_\xi\{\Lambda_n^*(t)>\Lambda_n(t)\}
+U\,P_\xi\{\Lambda_n^*(t)=\Lambda_n(t)\}
\right],
\]
and invert \(p_n(t)>\alpha\), using \([0,1]\) when \(N_{11}=0\). Apply the identical construction to \((X,1-A,1-Y)\) for PS.

Audit the lower submodel without blanket certification. Use \(X\sim{\rm Unif}([0,1]^p)\), \(A\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently, and conditional monotone types
\[
P(Y(0),Y(1)=(1,1)\mid X)=2(1-t)d,\quad
P((0,1)\mid X)=2td,\quad
P((0,0)\mid X)=1-2d.
\]
Then \(e=1/2\), \(m_0=2(1-t)d\), \(m_1=2d\), and the four observed cells are
\[
\left(d,(1-t)d,\frac12-d,\frac12-(1-t)d\right).
\]
For \(0<d\le\min(\bar d,1/2)\), this verifies consistency, ignorability, monotonicity, overlap when \(\varepsilon\le1/2\), bounded design density when \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), and Hölder membership when the balls contain constants. It does not by itself certify estimator-dependent remainder conditions, LR transfer, or score nondegeneracy. Verify nondegeneracy only for the local lower-bound pair \(t=1/2\pm h\min\{1,(nd)^{-1/2}\}\); it fails at the deterministic endpoint \(t=1\). State lower-bound membership only in the structural causal/Hölder class containing that local pair.

(2) The root fix is reachable for the finite rare-count experiment and for the Gaussian sub-regime (G), because the displayed score identity and variance bound derive the nuisance remainder from primitive Hölder laws and the named spline learner without pointwise rare localization. The exact obstruction to all-sequence recovery is fixed smoothness: \(s_0<1/2\), so one may choose \(d_n=n^{-b}\) with \(b<1\) but \(b\ge2s_0\); then \(nd_n\to\infty\) while \(a_{0,n}/\sqrt{d_n}\not\to0\), and the centered plug-in fluctuation is not \(o_P(\sqrt{d_n/n})\). If \(s_e+s_0\le1/2\), even the product bias cannot be negligible at regular \(d_n\). Therefore the continuous-law all-sequence Gaussian frontier is not derivable with fixed-order first-order spline learning; claiming it would require higher-order/adaptive structure, whereas exact randomized finite-support coverage and the bounded-count constant frontier remain valid without strengthening ignorability, monotonicity, or overlap.

D-1 ANGLE-1 V3 MATHEMATICAL REVISION DIRECTIVE — RECURRING WRONG PIVOT, NOT CONVERGENCE. The v3 reviewer is mathematically correct that `ass:propensity-estimability` and `ass:control-estimability` are nonstandard, redundant, and unsupported by Chernozhukov et al. as stated, but the review is incomplete: v3 has restored three structures expressly ruled out by the prior root fix—estimator-dependent class membership, pointwise rare localization, and an all-sequence Gaussian implication from \(nd_n\to\infty\). Delete `ass:propensity-estimability`, `ass:control-estimability`, `ass:rare-localization`, \(\omega_n\), \(C_\omega\), and every constraint \(e_\beta(x_i)u_i\le C_\omega d(\xi)\), including their appearances in the full class, LAN class, learning lemma, finite profiling domain, and lower-submodel membership claim. The primitive observed-law architecture must consist only of row-wise i.i.d. sampling, bounded design density \(c_X\le f_{X,n}\le C_X\), overlap \(\varepsilon\le e_n\le1-\varepsilon\), fixed \(p,\beta_e,\beta_0,L_e,L_0\), Hölder membership \(e_n\in\mathcal H^{\beta_e}(L_e)\), \(m_{0,n}\in\mathcal H^{\beta_0}(L_0)\), \(0<d_n\le\bar d\), and an admitted full-data extension satisfying consistency, ignorability, and monotonicity.
